title: ‘Bring Back THE Boss’: Nvidia Employees Petition for Jensen Huang’s Return
gist: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO over multiple reported affairs (one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset), a vocal segment of Nvidia employees is lobbying the board to reinstate him; the crisis has erased $1 trillion in market value and triggered FBI and congressional probes plus export-control risk.

themes.theme: Nvidia leadership crisis: facts and fallout

insights.claim: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, who had led the company since 1993, resigned as CEO after acknowledging in an email to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, following reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset and a second alleged affair with a direct report.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Abrupt loss of the founder-CEO of the AI chip bellwether is a major key-person event for NVDA.

insights.claim: Reuters reported an alleged third affair involving yet another Nvidia employee after Huang's resignation, and Huang has not commented further since his initial email.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Continuing drip of allegations prolongs headline risk and governance overhang for Nvidia.

insights.claim: The Huang scandal has cost Nvidia about $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced, prompted investigations by US lawmakers and the FBI, and raised the prospect of new export controls on chips.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Quantifies the valuation hit and flags regulatory/export-control tail risk tied to the China intelligence angle.
insights.quote: The crisis has cost the company $1 trillion in market value
insights.locator: Nvidia’s board is largely made up

insights.claim: Nvidia's board, largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang's longtime confidants, named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and appointed former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as board chair.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Interim leadership is a finance executive, not a product visionary; investors should watch for a permanent CEO search.
insights.locator: Nvidia’s board is largely made up

insights.claim: An internal Nvidia suggestion-box post by a longtime engineer, urging the board to weigh employee sentiment before acting, has drawn more than 1,600 comments, several asking the board to bring Huang back.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Signals strong internal loyalty to Huang and potential retention/morale risk under new leadership.

insights.claim: Roughly two dozen Nvidia employees posted support for Huang on LinkedIn in the hours after his resignation, while WIRED could not identify any employee posts supporting the resignation.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: One-sided public employee sentiment suggests the board's decision is unpopular internally.
insights.locator: It’s been business as usual inside

insights.claim: Some Nvidia employees believe the company will eventually suffer without its founder at the helm and perceive the desire for Huang's reinstatement as widespread.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Founder-dependence narrative frames the key investor question: can Nvidia sustain execution post-Huang?
insights.quote: Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen
insights.locator: One employee who has been at Nvidia

insights.claim: Many Nvidia employees had expected a board investigation to conclude before major changes, but Huang left just as the inquiry had begun, leaving staff seeking to understand why.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Opaque process and abrupt timing raise governance and transparency questions for shareholders.
insights.quote: Instead, Huang left just as the inquiry had begun.

insights.claim: Despite the shock, operations inside Nvidia have reportedly continued as business as usual during the week of the resignation.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Near-term operational disruption appears limited even as leadership is in flux.
insights.locator: It’s been business as usual inside
